- Function definitions (`pkgver()` and `package()`)

This is standard practice for AUR packages and does not involve any malicious activity. There are no shell injection vectors, unauthorized downloads, or attempts to execute untrusted code during the parsing phase.

All file operations are confined to the package directory (`$pkgdir`), and no sensitive data (passwords, keys, secrets) is referenced or manipulated. The `sha256sums` are fully specified (none are SKIPped), confirming the archive integrity checks are present.

Therefore, `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe to run—it will only parse and execute benign top-level PKGBUILD code.
</details>
